189: Rabbi Abba said to him, "Was that all?" He began and said, "The word of the Lord came to the priest Ezekiel son of Buzi, by the Chebar Canal, in the land of the Chaldeans (Ezekiel 1:3). There are three difficulties here. One is that we learned [that] the divine presence does not dwell outside of the land [of Israel]. Another is that he was not as trusted as Moses, about whom it is written: he is trusted throughout My household (Numbers 12:7). [Yet] he revealed and publicized all of the treasures of the King. Still another one is that he appears like someone who does not have a complete mind.

However, this is what we have concluded in our learning: God forbid! Ezekiel was a fine prophet and he revealed everything that he revealed with the permission of the Holy One, blessed be He. And he needed to reveal and publicize all of it, twice as much as what he revealed. As we have learned thus — one who is used to enduring pain, etc. (see above Zohar, Shemot 2:7 to 2:12). So it was all needed. And the Holy One, blessed be He has forever not left the Jewish people in exile without coming to set up His domicile with them. All the more so with Jacob. As he descended into exile, the Holy One, blessed be He, and his divine presence and the holy beings on high (and below) and the chariots all descended with Jacob. That is [the meaning of] what is written: who came to Egypt with Jacob (Exodus 1:1)."
